prerequisites: Basic knowledge of algebra and trigonometry
Elements of mathematical analysis: differentiation and integration of continuous functions in a real variable

learning_outcomes.text: The student will acquire knowledge of the basic concepts and fundamental laws of Classical Mechanics and Thermodynamics.
The student will learn to formalize into equations the laws governing the behavior of simple mechanical and thermodynamic systems, solving proposed problems based on input parameters.
The student will critically develop the analysis of results, checking their consistency in terms of dimensional analysis and self-consistency in numerical terms.
The student will carry out laboratory activities where they will become familiar with the main issues concerning the measurement of physical quantities.

The student will compare the results of the measurements taken with theoretical predictions, evaluating their consistency based on experimental errors affecting the measurements, and based on acquired knowledge related to the statistical treatment of random errors and the presence of possible systematic errors.

syllabus_topics: Dynamics of a point particle: Newton's three laws
General concepts of relative motion and reference frames
Momentum, impulse of force, impulse theorem, conservation of momentum
Work, kinetic energy, kinetic energy theorem, conservative forces, potential energy, conservation of mechanical energy, energy balance with dissipative forces
Theorems of motion of the center of mass, angular momentum, and energy
Work of internal and external forces
Rigid body: moment of inertia, Huygens-Steiner theorem, translational and rotational dynamics
Collision phenomena: elastic and inelastic collisions
Fluids: pressure, elements of fluid statics and dynamics
Thermodynamics: Thermodynamic systems and variables, equilibrium states, equation of state
Thermodynamic cycles, heat engines and refrigerators
Elements of kinetic theory of ideal gases
teaching_methods: Use of teaching technologies (Moodle and/or other teaching tools, software, videos, quizzes, Wooclap)
assessment_rules: The exam normally consists of a written test followed by an oral test, complemented by a mandatory test on laboratory activities. The written test is not mandatory if the two in-progress tests taken during the course period are passed. The oral test is not mandatory if the evaluation of the written test or the average of the in-progress tests exceeds a certain threshold. More details will be provided in class. Formative assessment through multiple-choice tests with immediate feedback is also provided to help students check their preparation level.
